controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where TESS saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · April and May 2025, mapped in this project
controls.notes: ROXs 42B A in its own color, darker where its light in TESS's images of April and May 2025 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 19.9 hours its light rose and fell by 13%. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 13% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · TESS mission light curve, sector 91
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in TESS sector 91, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 13% as it turned once in 19.9 hours. The light curve is the mission's own; the criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) decide that it shows the star turning, and starry finds the map that reproduces it. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color of a blackbody at the star's published temperature. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of a 3,650 K blackbody, Inglis et al.'s (2024) model temperature for this star from the pair's blended optical spectrum, modelled as the sum of the two stars.

physical.credit: Model radius at the Gaia distance of the unresolved pair; photometric mass; no measured rotation axis (display convention)
